dominant_strengths: Stacked book-spines metaphor turns a catalog into a tactile object, with each spine typeset in its book's own native voice
Exceptional craft visibility: kintsugi-style cracked spine, foil-stamped logos, and material textures convey print-quality fidelity on screen
Dark void backdrop plus tiny left-rail navigation lets the catalog itself become the entire visual hierarchy
dominant_weaknesses: Behavioral affordances are weak—tiny tick-mark nav and lone '?' glyph give little cue that spines are clickable or what each control does
Vertical spine stack forces a long scroll with no overview, filtering, or way to scan titles by topic or year
Per-spine typography variance, while charming, sacrifices scannability when users want to quickly locate a specific book
fix_priorities: Add hover/active states and labels on the left rail so navigation legibility matches the catalog's craft
Provide a secondary 'index' or grid view for fast title lookup without abandoning the hero stack
Introduce subtle parallax or lift on spine hover to confirm interactivity before click
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective dominate through tactile bookcraft and curatorial gravitas, while behavioral usability lags behind cryptic micro-controls.
rationale.intent_fit: Strongly fits the Stripe Press brief—publishing-as-physical-artifact rendered with rare digital craft, even if utility is sacrificed for atmosphere.
